olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A positive integer is \textit{tico} if it is the product of three distinct primes summing to 74. Verify 2014 is tico. Find the next tico year and the last tico year ever.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2014

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Cyclic trapezoid $ABCD$ with $AB\parallel CD$, center $O$; $P=BC\cap AD$. Circle through $O,P$ meets $BC,AD$ at interior points $F,G$. Show $BF=DG$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2014

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Real $a,b,c,d$ with no two equal, $\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{c}+\frac{c}{d}+\frac{d}{a}=4$, and $ac=bd$. Find the maximum of $\frac{a}{c}+\frac{b}{d}+\frac{c}{a}+\frac{d}{b}$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2014

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A stair figure is built in stages: stage 1 has 1 square, stage 2 has 5, etc. (each stage $k$ has $\frac{k^2+k}{2}\cdot 2-1$ or similar). Find the last stage with fewer than 2014 squares.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2014

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Points $A,B,C,D$ on a line in order with $AB,CD>BC$. Equilateral triangles $APB$, $BCQ$, $CDR$ on the same side of $AD$ with $\angle PQR=120^\circ$. Show $\dfrac{1}{AB}+\dfrac{1}{CD}=\dfrac{1}{BC}$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2014

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $n$ is \textit{funny} if for every positive divisor $d$ of $n$, $d+2$ is prime. Find all funny numbers with the largest possible number of divisors.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2014
